style: STYLE (applies to every image): dark-field light microscopy of living microbes, as a stylised video game. Pure black background. Cells are translucent glowing bodies with a bright rim and a darker, glassy interior, with soft light bloom and a subtle circular lens vignette at the picture edges. Strict four-colour stain palette: crystal violet (#8B5CF6 purple) for native life, safranin pink (#FF5C8A) for the player's disguised robot cells, iodine amber (#F5A524) for waste and chemicals, malachite green (#2DD4A7) for immune activity. Fine floating dust specks and faint out-of-focus bokeh discs in the far background. Clean, elegant, slightly cute, never gory or frightening. No photorealistic lab equipment unless asked. No watermark, no signature, no extra text beyond what is asked for.

requests.prompt: Establishing style frame for a video game called Look Alive. A dark-field microscope view of a Petri dish world. Hundreds of glowing purple rod-shaped native bacteria drift in loose clusters across a black field. Among them, on the right of centre, is a small colony of about forty round pink cells that look almost the same as the natives but are subtly too neat and evenly spaced. Thin wisps of amber haze trail from a few cells. The view is wide, calm and beautiful, like a deep-sea photograph. No user interface, no text.

Title screen for the video game LOOK ALIVE, in the same style as the attached image. In the centre, large glowing letters spell exactly: LOOK ALIVE. The letters are made of softly glowing pink cells packed together, and the letter I in ALIVE is a single rod-shaped bacterium with a faint hexagonal seam pattern showing through its skin. Around the title, purple native bacteria drift on a black field. Below the title, a small cream paper specimen label, like a museum slide label, with neat handwriting that reads exactly: Bacillus normalis - not a robot. Nothing else is written.

Gameplay screenshot mock-up in the same style as the attached image. The circular dark-field dish view fills the left two thirds: purple native rods and a small pink colony. On the right is a slim, dark, minimal interface panel with thin glowing lines: at the top a horizontal gauge with a green safe zone in the middle and red zones at both ends, with a small marker in the green; below it four small dial needles in a column, each with a tiny icon; below that a line graph showing a pink population line staying inside a dashed horizontal band. Interface text is tiny and can be illegible placeholder marks; do not write readable sentences. Elegant scientific-instrument look.

Same style as the attached image, but zoomed far out so individual cells are too small to see. The whole circular Petri dish is visible as a glowing disc on black. Native life appears as soft purple clouds and veins of light like a nebula or a city seen from orbit; one small pink glowing patch sits among them; faint amber haze pools in places. The rim of the dish is a thin bright ring. No text, no interface.

Extreme close-up in the same style as the attached image. Two cells side by side fill the frame. On the left, a purple native bacterium: organic, slightly lumpy, asymmetrical, with wobbly internal granules and a wavy flagellum. On the right, a pink disguised robot cell: nearly the same shape, but on close inspection its skin shows a faint regular hexagonal seam pattern and its internal granules are arranged in a tidy grid. The difference is subtle and funny. No text.

The dramatic moment of exposure, same style as the attached image. A pink colony of cells in the centre of a dark-field dish. A bright ring of light sweeps outward across them; inside the ring the round pink cells have resolved into crisp glowing hexagonal tiles with visible seams, like a honeycomb of tiny machines; outside the ring they still look like soft organic blobs. Purple native rods nearby recoil slightly. No text.

Same style as the attached image. Stage one of the planet's immune response: curiosity. A small pink colony sits among purple natives. Three or four large, soft, green amoeba-like immune cells are drifting slowly toward the pink colony from the edges, each with a single pale eye-like nucleus turned toward it, like polite but nosy neighbours. The mood is tense and slightly comic, not scary. No text.

Same style as the attached image. Stage three of the immune response: a dense swarm of glowing green immune cells surrounds and engulfs a pink colony whose cells now show obvious hexagonal seams. Green tendrils wrap the pink cells. Purple natives keep their distance at the edges. Dramatic but clean and bloodless, like a school of fish closing in. No text.

Same style as the attached image. The scouting phase: a circular scanning lens, drawn as a thin bright ring with small tick marks around it, hovers over a cluster of purple native bacteria. Inside the lens the natives are shown in sharper focus, with thin pale callout lines leading to three tiny abstract readout icons (a small bar gauge, a droplet, a waveform). Outside the lens the view is slightly dimmer. Readouts are icons and tick marks only, no readable words.

Build screen mock-up for the game, same style as the attached image. On the left, a large portrait of one pink robot cell in dark field. On the right, a minimal dark panel with two horizontal see-saw sliders, each with a small pictogram at either end (splitting cell versus thick shell; lightning bolt versus wobbly line), a small circular dial, and below them one card with rounded corners showing a two-part sentence frame made of two coloured chips (one blue, one orange) joined by an arrow. All labels are abstract placeholder marks, no readable sentences. Elegant instrument-panel look.

Failure autopsy screen, same style as the attached image. A frozen dark-field view of a pink colony surrounded by green immune cells, treated like an annotated lab slide: two thin hand-drawn white chalk arrows point at specific pink cells and at an amber waste cloud, each ending in a small handwritten scribble (illegible placeholder handwriting). Along the bottom, a thin timeline bar with a single red pin on it. In one corner a cream paper tag stamped in red ink with the words exactly: COVER BLOWN.

Win screen, same style as the attached image. A calm dark-field dish where pink cells mingle unnoticed among purple natives. Over the lower right corner lies a cream paper specimen card, slightly rotated, with a large green ink rubber stamp across it reading exactly: SUFFICIENTLY BACTERIAL. The stamp ink is slightly uneven like a real rubber stamp. No other readable text.

A message from the handler, same style as the attached image for the background. A sheet of cream office letterhead paper lies at a slight angle over a dark-field dish. The letterhead has a small simple logo of a hexagon with an eye in it and a printed header reading exactly: DEPARTMENT OF PLAUSIBLE DENIABILITY. The body of the letter is a few lines of neat typewriter text that are too small to read (placeholder lines). There is a coffee cup ring stain on one corner and a red stamp reading exactly: BE COOL.

Planet one, Acidica, same style as the attached image. A dark-field dish where purple native sour-rod bacteria each trail a thin plume of amber waste haze, so the whole field has drifting amber ribbons like smoke in still air. Small amber-green scavenger cells graze along the ribbons. A small pink colony in one corner has no amber trail yet, and it stands out for that reason. No text.

Planet two, Quietus, same style as the attached image. A dark-field dish where every purple native cell emits thin concentric signal rings, like ripples from raindrops on a pond, overlapping across the whole field in a steady rhythm. A small pink colony near the centre emits no rings at all and sits in a conspicuous patch of stillness. No text.

Planet three, Brightside, same style as the attached image. A dark-field dish crossed by two wide diagonal shafts of pale white light. Purple native cells crowd into the dark bands between the light shafts and avoid the lit areas, which are empty. A few pink cells are drifting carelessly into the light, glowing a little too brightly. No text.

Planet four, Mycelia Prime, same style as the attached image. A dark-field dish covered by a delicate branching network of glowing purple fungal threads (hyphae) with bright nodes where threads meet, like a map of rivers or neurons. Small beads of light travel along the threads. A few pink cells have attached thin pink threads to the edge of the network. No text.

Planet five, Tidewash, same style as the attached image. A dark-field dish where the whole population of purple native cells is streaming in one direction in long curved bands, like a murmuration of starlings or a tide, with motion-blur streaks behind them. A small pink colony is standing still in the flow, with the stream parting around it. No text.

A character reference sheet on a black background, same style as the attached image. Three versions of the same pink robot cell in a row, evenly spaced, each about the same size. Left: fully organic-looking, round, soft and slightly lumpy. Middle: mostly organic, but with a faint hexagonal seam pattern beginning to show through one side. Right: fully exposed, a crisp hexagonal mechanical cell with glowing seams and a tidy grid of internal parts. Under each, a tiny simple icon only: a tick, a wavy line, and an exclamation mark. No words.

A character reference sheet on a black background, same style as the attached image. Six different native alien microbe species in a two-row grid, all in purple with small accents of amber or green: a plump rod, a chain of beads, a comma-shaped swimmer with a tail, a star-shaped cell with soft spikes, a flat ruffled disc, and a spiral. Each is charming and clearly organic and irregular. Evenly spaced, no overlap, no text.

A colour and material board for the game, same style as the attached image. On a black background, four large glowing glass droplets in a row: purple, pink, amber and green. Under each droplet is a small sample: under purple, three native cells; under pink, three robot cells; under amber, a wisp of haze; under green, one immune cell. Below that, a thin horizontal strip of four flat colour swatches in the same order. Minimal and elegant like a designer's style tile. No words.

Logo design for the video game LOOK ALIVE, same style as the attached image. On a plain black background, a clean wordmark in a round, friendly sans-serif reading exactly: LOOK ALIVE. The two letter O shapes in LOOK are a pair of round glowing cells that read like eyes, one purple and organic, one pink with a faint hexagonal pattern. The rest of the letters are a pale glowing white with a slight bright rim. Centred, generous margins, nothing else in the picture.

An icon sheet for the game on a black background, same style as the attached image. Eight simple glowing line icons in a two-row grid, each inside a thin circle, drawn with rounded strokes in pale white with one stain-colour accent: a cell splitting in two; a cell with a thick shell; a lightning bolt in a cell; a wobbly irregular line; a droplet with fumes; a cluster of cells in a blob of slime; a cell emitting signal rings; a cell wearing a mask. Consistent stroke weight, evenly spaced, no words.

An interface element sheet on a black background, same style as the attached image. Four semicircular dial gauges in a row, each with a thin glowing needle, a softly pulsing shaded safe zone in the middle of its arc, and a small pictogram above it: a rising curve, a droplet, a small broken cell, and a metronome. Each gauge has a different fill pattern in its arc (stripes, dots, crosshatch, zigzag) so they can be told apart without colour. Thin elegant scientific-instrument lines. No words.

Level-select screen, same style as the attached image. A dark wall with a grid of about fifteen small circular Petri dishes seen from above, each glowing softly with its own tiny colony pattern in purple with touches of pink, amber or green. A few dishes are bright and detailed (completed), a few are dim and empty (locked). Thin lines connect them like a constellation path. No readable text.

A retro travel postcard, slightly rotated, lying on a black background. The postcard picture is a dark-field microscope view in the same style as the attached image: an alien dish landscape of purple native cells with amber ribbons. Across the picture in cheerful retro postcard lettering it reads exactly: GREETINGS FROM ACIDICA. In the corner is a small postage stamp showing a pink cell wearing a tiny disguise moustache. Cream card border with slightly worn edges.

Key art for the game's store page, same style as the attached image. A single large circular microscope view is split down the middle by a thin vertical line. On the left half, a crowd of round glowing cells that all look alike and organic, purple with a few pink ones blending in. On the right half, the very same scene, but the pink cells are revealed as crisp hexagonal machines with glowing seams while the purple ones stay organic. Strong, simple, readable at thumbnail size. No text.

Same scene type as the attached image, but shown through the immune system's eyes: the picture is almost monochrome pale grey-green on black, natives are faint calm outlines, and the cells that behave abnormally glow hot red-orange with small alert brackets around them, like a thermal camera or a targeting view. About a third of the pink colony is flagged this way. Thin scan lines sweep across. No words.

A concept for a later chapter of the game, same style as the attached image. The life here is larger and plant-like: glowing purple chains of rectangular algae cells and branching filaments with small green chloroplast dots inside, drifting in dark water. Hidden among them are a few pink filaments that are slightly too straight and evenly segmented. Wide, serene composition. No text.

Same style as the attached image, showing the invisible chemistry of the dish made visible: soft translucent fields of colour flow between the cells like aurora or ink in water. Amber clouds of waste spread from cell clusters, pale blue-white food gradients fade from one edge, and thin green signal ripples pass through. Purple natives and a small pink colony sit inside these flowing fields. Beautiful, scientific, like a weather map of a tiny world. No text.
